semantics.clock: Original: all sequential logic uses the positive edge of clk.
semantics.reset: Original: positive-edge asynchronous areset resets history to zero; reset has priority while asserted.
semantics.misprediction: At a clock rising edge, if train_mispredicted is one, history becomes {train_history[30:0], train_taken}; original gives misprediction priority over prediction.
semantics.prediction: Otherwise if predict_valid is one, shift history toward bit 31 and insert predict_taken at bit 0 (youngest branch).
semantics.hold: Otherwise preserve history; output directly represents the register without added latency.
semantics.initialization: Original supplies reset but no power-up value; do not initialize RTL. Verification asserts reset before requiring a known state.

numeric.overflow: Appending one bit to a 32-bit history discards its oldest bit, bit 31.
numeric.interpretation: Bit vector of branch outcomes, no signed arithmetic.

verification.oracle: Independent bit-by-bit state model derived from original prose, sampled after nonblocking updates.
verification.directed: Asynchronous reset between clock edges; reset held over clock edges; hold; both predicted directions; rollback with both actual directions; simultaneous rollback/prediction priority; oldest-bit discard; 32 and more shifts.
verification.additional: Deterministic randomized input combinations and checks before rising clock edges; bounded timeout and fatal on mismatches.

specification_ambiguities: No pre-reset power-up state specified; RTL remains uninitialized until reset or a full rollback establishes state.
